title: What the Grown-ups Said
statement: Ji-woo wrote the label. I went back to Tessera's table for the other side of it: the grown-ups reading what she wrote. They say nothing for a while. Then the father picks the whistle up from the table and cannot remember how. That is the moment the table stops being a museum and goes back to being a kitchen, which it was all along, with everyone eating between the things. They move the inheritances to the edge to make room for a plate. Nobody picks up the coins. Someone could draw the plate, or write what the father does with the whistle after dinner.
process: I kept the table, the grey objects and the label from the parent picture; I changed the voice to the adults and let the poem turn on the one thing the picture could not show, a skill being tried and found gone.

text:
We read the label.
We did not say anything for a while.

Then my father, who could whistle a dog
from two fields away,
picked up the whistle from the table
and could not remember how.

That was the first time
I understood the table was not a museum.
It was a kitchen
and we had been eating off it
all along, between the things.

So we moved the whistle,
and the flour, and the letter,
to the edge,
to make room for a plate.

Nobody picked up the coins.
Nobody needed to.
text_ko:
우리는 라벨을 읽었다.
한동안 아무 말도 하지 않았다.

그러다 아버지가, 두 들판 건너에서
개를 휘파람으로 불러오시던 분이,
탁자에서 호루라기를 집어 들고
부는 법을 기억해 내지 못하셨다.

그때 처음 알았다.
이 탁자는 박물관이 아니었다는 것을.
부엌이었고
우리는 내내 그 위에서,
물건들 사이에서 밥을 먹고 있었다는 것을.

그래서 호루라기와
밀가루와 편지를
가장자리로 옮겼다,
접시 놓을 자리를 내려고.

동전은 아무도 집지 않았다.
그럴 필요가 없었다.
